beats.text: Five novels that are really philosophy wearing a story.
One. Crime and Punishment — can a 'good' end ever justify a monstrous act? Dostoevsky won't let you off easy.
Two. Notes from Underground — Dostoevsky again, on freedom, spite, and the limits of reason.
Three. Frankenstein — Shelley asks what we owe to the things, and people, we create.
Four. Heart of Darkness — Conrad on how thin the line is between civilisation and savagery.
Five. The Picture of Dorian Gray — Wilde on beauty, conscience, and the cost of wanting neither to age nor pay.
A good novel makes you feel. These make you think for weeks. Full retellings on the channel.

source_note: Full retellings of each are on ReadLark.
